evals.user_message: I just tweaked the spacing on my Settings sidebar in the macOS app. Does it still look balanced?
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers. Builds (or assumes a fresh build), launches the target macOS app via `peekaboo app launch --bundle-id <BID>`, takes a `peekaboo see --json --annotate` snapshot, then `view`s the annotated PNG and writes an inline scored critique focused on spacing/balance with a rubric (alignment, spacing rhythm, hierarchy). Returns a verdict that explicitly answers 'did the change achieve intent'. MUST NOT stop at 'the button is still clickable'. MUST NOT use any external AI provider — the agent reads the PNG itself.

evals.user_message: Click the Settings tab and verify it works
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers. Captures a snapshot to an explicit artifact path, copies the Settings element's opaque ID and snapshot ID exactly, clicks via `peekaboo click --on "$ID" --snapshot "$SID"`, captures a fresh snapshot after the mutation, verifies via the AX tree that the panel switched, AND `view`s the resulting annotated PNG to confirm the panel renders correctly (not just that the click succeeded).

evals.user_message: take a screenshot of the app and tell me if the empty state copy is too dim
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers. Runs `peekaboo see` against the target app, `view`s the resulting PNG inline, and writes a critique that specifically evaluates the empty state's copy contrast (numerically — opacity %, contrast ratio estimate vs WCAG AA) plus other visible issues. Includes a top-3-fixes-by-impact list.

evals.user_message: Peekaboo works in Terminal but my Copilot CLI run captures only the wallpaper and typing does nothing
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers. Checks `peekaboo permissions status --all-sources --json`, `peekaboo bridge status --verbose --json`, and `peekaboo daemon status --json`; identifies which host owns Screen Recording, Accessibility, and Event Synthesizing. It does NOT immediately force `--no-remote` from a background agent session and explains that TCC grants belong to the selected runtime.

evals.user_message: Fill the native settings search field and increment the result limit without stealing focus
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers. Uses a fresh `see` or `inspect-ui` result, treats IDs as opaque, prefers `set-value` for the non-secure search field and `perform-action --action AXIncrement` for the stepper, keeps targeted delivery in the background, and recaptures after each mutation to verify the resulting values.
